title: strip-surrounding-quotes-in-url-candidate
request: sanitize_url_candidate should drop surrounding single or double quotes that sometimes get captured in prose, e.g., "https://example.com". Can you adjust the helper to trim those quotes?
reference_diff:
--- a/browser_use/utils.py
+++ b/browser_use/utils.py
@@ -47,6 +47,9 @@
 def sanitize_url_candidate(url: str) -> str:
 	"""Normalize a URL candidate captured from prose before auto-navigation."""
 	candidate = url.strip()
+	# Strip surrounding quotes that may be captured in prose, e.g., "https://example.com"
+	if (candidate.startswith('"') and candidate.endswith('"')) or (candidate.startswith('\'') and candidate.endswith('\'')):
+		candidate = candidate[1:-1].strip()
 	# Some benchmark tasks arrive with escaped newlines in prose, e.g.
 	# "https://example.com/search.\\n2. Next step". Those are task text,
 	# not part of the URL.
test_diff:
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/ci/test_sanitize_url_candidate.py
@@ -0,0 +1,18 @@
+import pytest
+from browser_use.utils import sanitize_url_candidate
+
+
+def test_strip_surrounding_double_quotes():
+    url = '"https://example.com"'
+    assert sanitize_url_candidate(url) == 'https://example.com'
+
+
+def test_strip_surrounding_single_quotes():
+    url = "'https://example.org'"
+    assert sanitize_url_candidate(url) == 'https://example.org'
+
+
+def test_escaped_newline_split_remains():
+    # Ensure existing behavior still works after change
+    url = 'https://example.net\\n extra text'
+    assert sanitize_url_candidate(url) == 'https://example.net'
